business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business, 10-K MD&A, and 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Porch operates four reportable segments since January 2025: Insurance Services, Software & Data, Consumer Services (all owned by Porch, collectively called 'Porch Shareholder Interest'), and the Reciprocal Segment (managed but not owned by Porch, consolidated as a variable interest entity).
quotes: Beginning in January 2025, we operate under four reportable segments that are also our operating segments. Three of these segments are owned by Porch — Insurance Services, Software & Data, and Consumer Services. We collectively call these three segments, along with corporate functions, the "Porch Shareholder Interest." Our fourth segment, the Reciprocal Segment, is managed, but not owned, by Porch and, at this time, is consolidated for reporting purposes.

business_model.claim: The Insurance Services segment earns management fees and commissions from the Reciprocal, receives policy fees from policyholders and lead fees from agencies, earns interest on surplus notes held by the Reciprocal, and includes a captive reinsurer for reinsurance support.
quotes: Our Insurance Services segment earns management fees from the Reciprocal in exchange for managing and operating its business. This segment also receives policy fees from policyholders, lead fees from agencies, earns interest on surplus notes from the Reciprocal, and includes a captive reinsurer to provide reinsurance support to improve capital efficiency for the Reciprocal.

business_model.claim: The Software & Data segment provides subscription and transactional software to inspection, mortgage, title, and roofing companies, and sells Home Factors property-insights data to insurance carriers and other third parties.
quotes: We provide software, on a subscription and predominantly transactional basis, to inspection, mortgage, title, and roofing companies.
Home Factors provides interior and exterior attributes and condition data to help insurance carriers improve underwriting, pricing, and risk selection.

business_model.claim: The Consumer Services segment sells home warranty products (whole-home, service line, extended labor) in 50 states and D.C., and provides moving-related services including movers, TV/Internet, and security.
quotes: Our Consumer Services segment provides warranty products through Porch Warranty and other warranty brands to protect the whole home. Our Consumer Services segment also provides moving related services such as movers, TV/Internet, and security.

competitive_position.claim: Porch faces competition from large insurance carriers, vertical software companies, home-services marketplaces, and property data companies across its multiple business lines.
quotes: We compete with, among others: (i) large insurance carriers (ii) vertical software companies in our markets, (iii) companies who provide or help consumers purchase homeowners insurance, home warranty, moving, and other home services, (iv) search engines or online marketplaces for all types of home services with which we assist consumers, (v) property and mover data companies, and (vi) other companies which help consumers to make managing and maintaining their homes simple.

Some of our competitors are well-established, have greater functional and compliance maturity, or have better competitive positions with respect to certain geographical areas, consumer and service provider demographics, and/or types of services offered.

competitive_position.claim: Catastrophe and severe-weather events, particularly in states where the Reciprocal has a concentration of policyholders, pose a material risk to the Reciprocal's results and to Porch's revenue from management fees.
quotes: The incidence, frequency and severity of weather events, extensive wildfires, and other catastrophes, particularly occurring where the Porch Reciprocal Exchange (the "Reciprocal") has a concentration of homeowners insurance policyholders, or that adversely impact consumer confidence and spending behavior in the industries we serve, could have a material effect on our results of operations and financial condition.

A single catastrophe event, or a series of events, could produce claims that exceed the combined reserves, reinsurance recoveries, and capital resources available to the Reciprocal and the acquired businesses.

the pending acquisition by Homeowners of America Holding Corporation ("HOA Holdco") and Porch Insurance Reciprocal Exchange (the "Reciprocal") of Allied Trust Insurance Company ("ATIC"), Allied Underwriters LLC ("AU MGA"), and Lonestar Lagniappe Reinsurance Holdings, LLC ("Lonestar") pursuant to the Stock and Membership Interest Purchase Agreement, dated as of October 13, 2026
If the Acquisition has not been completed by April 1, 2027, as such date may be extended, either party may terminate the Purchase Agreement

material_events.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A for the year ended December 31, 2025 (P3)
material_events.claim: Porch completed a series of privately negotiated refinancing transactions: exchanged $96.8 million aggregate principal of 0.75% Convertible Senior Unsecured Notes due 2026 for $83.0 million of newly issued 9.00% Convertible Senior Unsecured Notes due 2030, issued an additional $51.0 million of 2030 Notes for cash, and repurchased $47.5 million of 2026 Notes for $47.3 million in cash.
quotes: On May 27, 2025, we completed a series of privately negotiated refinancing transactions with certain holders of our 0.75% Convertible Senior Unsecured Notes due in September 2026 (the "2026 Notes").
Exchanged $96.8 million aggregate principal amount of 2026 Notes for $83.0 million aggregate principal amount of newly issued 9.00% Convertible Senior Unsecured Notes due 2030 (the "2030 Notes")
Issued an additional $51.0 million aggregate principal amount of 2030 Notes for cash to the same investors that participated in the exchange
Repurchased $47.5 million aggregate principal amount of 2026 Notes for $47.3 million in cash

material_events.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 Business (P1) and 10-K MD&A Recent Developments (P3) for the year ended December 31, 2025
material_events.claim: Porch completed the formation of Porch Reciprocal Exchange and sold its legacy homeowners insurance carrier, Homeowners of America (HOA), to the Reciprocal for a purchase price of approximately $105 million (HOA's estimated surplus at December 31, 2024) less $58 million of principal and unpaid interest under a prior surplus note, financed by a surplus note from the Reciprocal to Porch bringing total surplus notes to approximately $106 million.
quotes: In January 2025, we completed the formation of Porch Reciprocal Exchange (the "Reciprocal") and, as part of this process, sold our legacy homeowners insurance carrier, Homeowners of America ("HOA"), to the Reciprocal.

we completed the sale of our homeowners insurance carrier, Homeowners of America ("HOA"), to the Reciprocal for a purchase price equal to HOA's estimated surplus at December 31, 2024, of approximately $105 million, less $58 million of principal and unpaid interest under a surplus note issued by HOA to Porch in 2023
bringing the total surplus notes held by Porch to approximately $106 million

risks.basis: stated in P5 (10-Q Risk Factors) and P8 (8-K press release)
risks.claim: The Allied Trust acquisition requires approvals from the Texas Department of Insurance and other regulators, and if not completed by April 1, 2027, either party may terminate the Purchase Agreement.
quotes: Completion of the Acquisition is subject to conditions, including the receipt of required approvals from the Texas Department of Insurance and other applicable insurance regulators, the absence of any legal restraint, and the accuracy of representations and the performance of covenants by the parties.
If the Acquisition has not been completed by April 1, 2027, as such date may be extended, either party may terminate the Purchase Agreement

risks.basis: stated in P5 (10-Q Risk Factors) and P8 (8-K press release); reinsurance structure from P3 (10-K MD&A)
risks.claim: The Allied Trust acquisition increases catastrophe exposure concentration in Louisiana and the Gulf Coast, where a single event could produce claims exceeding combined reserves, reinsurance recoveries, and capital.
quotes: The acquired businesses write residential property insurance in states exposed to hurricanes, windstorms, hail, severe weather events, and other catastrophe events, with a significant concentration in Louisiana and along the Gulf Coast.

A single catastrophe event, or a series of events, could produce claims that exceed the combined reserves, reinsurance recoveries, and capital resources available to the Reciprocal and the acquired businesses.

risks.basis: stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors) and P5 (10-Q Risk Factors)
risks.claim: Reinsurance may become unavailable at current levels and prices, limiting the Reciprocal's ability to write new business and exposing it to counterparty risk.
quotes: Reinsurance may be unavailable at current levels and prices, which may limit the Reciprocal's ability to write new business. Furthermore, reinsurance subjects the Reciprocal to counterparty risk and may not be adequate to protect it against losses, which could have a material effect on results of our operations and financial condition.

The combined policyholder count and geographic concentration may cause reinsurers to require higher premiums, higher attachment points or retentions, reduced limits, or less favorable terms when existing programs are renewed or new programs are placed for the combined operations, and reinsurance may not be available on acceptable terms or at all.

quotes: As of April 1, 2025, coverage for excess of loss catastrophe reinsurance starts at $25.0 million per occurrence up to a loss of $410.0 million. Additionally, the third-party quota share reinsurance contracts start immediately at 7.5% of property and casualty ("P&C") losses, which includes catastrophe events, bringing the effective retention for the Reciprocal from $25.0 million per occurrence to $23.1 million per occurrence.

our captive reinsurance entity provides reinsurance coverage for risks with low earnings volatility, such as non-catastrophic weather quota share, in order to create more capital efficiency at the Reciprocal.

The Reciprocal is a separate legal entity, owned by its member policyholders, and is not owned, wholly or in part, by the Company. The Reciprocal is consolidated in our financial statements solely as a result of the Company's variable interest in, and status as primary beneficiary of, the entity.
